title: Platform health stabilization playbook + sprint kickoff
summary: Quarterly health/checkin focused on a recent usage spike, right-sizing Dedicated vs Hosted, defining a stabilization sprint and deliverables. Customer emphasized need for SSO + KMS assurances and a short benchmark to validate latency for high-throughput routing. Agreed next step: Redwood to share tailored pricing, security pack, and a 2-week pilot plan with benchmark success criteria.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-19 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Luis (CSM), Samir (CTO), Hannah (Dir ML), Raj (SRE), Nia (Product)

Summary (auto): QBR-style checkin after a recent traffic surge. Focus on immediate stabilization (short sprint), cost levers (batching, quantization, routing), and security paperwork for wider adoption.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. Quick agenda — two big things: stabilize the service after last week's surge, and line up pilot + pricing so you can decide on Dedicated vs Hosted. Sound right?
[00:12] Samir (CTO): Yep, that's it. The spike caught us off guard, p95 latency went high and a couple of user flows timed out. We need a practical playbook not just a postmortem.
[00:22] Jordan (SE): yeah and hi all, i'll jump into the numbers in a bit. My focus will be on the KV cache behavior and batching config — those two gave us most wins on our tests.
[00:33] Hannah (Dir ML): quick thing — we also saw a small quality drift after we switched to an L1-quantized variant for cost reasons, not sure if that's related to the higher tail latencies.
[00:42] Raj (SRE): also we hit a quota throttling event in us-west-2 — some of the fallback logic routed to a smaller model and that caused a different tokenization path so our metrics were a little messy.

[00:55] Jordan (SE): Okay i'll try to unpack. On the latency: from what we saw, the main drivers were (1) a sudden qps increase at the 11:00 UTC window, (2) long sequences from the new feedback assistant, and (3) missed prefix cache warmups because requests were routed across AZs. Continuous batching helped but once p99 spikes hit, queues overflowed.
[01:20] Maya (AE): correct, so there are two levers — short term: routing and reserve burst + canary fallbacks; medium term: dedicate a reserved pool or tune batching and model variants. The tradeoff is cost vs p95.
[01:33] Samir: Our business constraint is we can't have >1% failed requests on the checkout flow. Cost is important but availability is the bright line.
[01:40] Maya: understood. That's typical. On security, we heard from procurement: SOC2 + SSO + KMS. Luis, you had the security doc ready?
[01:47] Luis (CSM): yes, we have a security pack — SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO guide, and KMS integration notes. I'll share the link after call: https://redwood.example.com/security/bluecliff-pack (placeholder).

[02:05] Nia (Product): For the pilot we want explicit success criteria: latency p95 < 300ms for the checkout path, cost per thousand tokens under $X, and no more than 0.5% fallback errors. We need those in writing.
[02:18] Maya: we'll put that into the SoW. Jordan will capture the benchmark steps.

[05:00] Jordan (SE): (screen share artifacts referenced) The benchmark we'll run includes: synthetic traffic replay (from Raj's profile), KV cache priming, mixed prompt sizes, and A/B between the quantized variant and full float baseline. The success matrix is p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per token.
[05:24] Raj (SRE): i'll send the traffic profile csv — FYI it includes a new long-context assistant mode that skewed seq length to median 1.2k tokens during peaks.

[08:12] Hannah: there's also governance questions. We need audit logs at request-level for 90 days, role-based access in the console, and the ability to rotate keys via our HSM. Can Redwood support HSM key wrapping?
[08:25] Jordan: yes we support KMS integrations, key wrapping via customer-managed KMS is possible — some of the early deploys used HSM-backed KMS. We'll validate with our infra team.
[08:40] Maya: i'll include a short note and include the compliance contacts. Luis will drop the SOC2 report.

[12:05] Samir: Another ask — can you give us a concrete delta in unit cost if we reserve Dedicated capacity with burst vs staying hosted? We need the model.
[12:15] Maya: Sure — high level: Dedicated reserve reduces per-token cost for stable baseline traffic by ~30-45% depending on utilization, but you trade commit. There's also the hybrid routing option: keep a hosted fallback for spikes. We'll model that in the pricing doc.
[12:31] Hannah: And how hard is it to move from Hosted -> Dedicated? We need low friction in case we want to flip.
[12:37] Jordan: We've built migration tooling and version pinning; the API remains the same so it's mostly infra setup and data plane routing. Canary rollouts and A/B are supported. We'll give a migration checklist.

[17:40] Luis: quick ops note — we can enable tracing hooks so you can correlate application traces with token-level latency. That helps root cause.
[17:50] Raj: that's huge for us.

[22:00] Maya: Recap of pilot timeline proposition: 2-week pilot, week 0 prep (traffic share, access), week 1 run benchmarks + tuning, week 2 validation + handoff. Success gates: p95 target, cost target, no security blockers.
[22:17] Samir: sounds good. Who owns the bench account?
[22:20] Jordan: Redwood will provision a dedicated test pool and we'll share credentials; Raj will run the replay from your infra or we can run it from ours — up to you. If you run from yours the network egress numbers are more realistic.

[29:05] Hannah: small technical question — the prefix cache invalidation you mentioned, does it behave differently on Dedicated?
[29:12] Jordan: same runtime semantics, but Dedicated lets you pin shards to reduce cross-AZ cache misses. Also rack affinity and colocated cache priming is easier with reserved pools.

[33:00] Samir: procurement asked about indemnity and data residency. We have EU customers. Is Redwood able to store logs in EU for EU traffic?
[33:12] Maya: Yes, we have region-level data residency options for Private/ Dedicated. We'll share the data flow and residency SLA in the security pack.

[40:00] Nia: on the product side, we'd like a short timeline for rolling the new assistant into production after pilot, estimate 3 sprints post-pilot if everything looks good — that's about 6 weeks.
[40:12] Maya: noted, we'll align pilot scoping to that timeline.

[45:10] Jordan: small gotcha we noticed in their traffic: a sudden shift to 1.5k token average increases KV cache pressure; we recommend a cache warmup schedule and prefix prioritization for the assistant. Also suggest lowering batching window for checkout to keep latency tight — tradeoff is throughput.
[45:33] Raj: we'll accept a slight throughput hit for the checkout path.

[52:00] Maya: Any other blockers?
[52:05] Samir: none from my side. Just make sure pricing has the burst options explicitly called out.
[52:12] Hannah: and include the regression checks for top 20 golden prompts.
[52:18] Luis: i'll coordinate the artifact drop — security pack, SOC2, SSO guide.

Closing (final minute)
[57:00] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pricing, benchmark plan, and pilot SoW. Next meeting — pilot kickoff — we'll shoot for 2026-08-25 or 26.
[57:20] Samir: thanks, talk soon.

Notes about transcript: occasional speaker attribution may be imperfect (Luis and Jordan overlapped at 17:50), some product names abbreviated. Links and artifacts to be shared after call.
